newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian opposition launches new rally.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian opposition launches new rally.

text.p: Bulgarian opposition supporters began a fresh rally on Saturday outside Sofia's gold-domed cathedral, after riot police put an end to their 10-hour siege of parliament.

State news agency BTA said 97 were injured in clashes between protesters and police, who fired blank cartridges and used clubs to beat a path from the parliament building for trapped deputies from the ruling Socialist party early on Saturday.
The agency said the injured comprised 85 civilians, including two parliamentary deputies from the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces, four security guards from parliament and eight police.
President Zhelyu Zhelev said he would not ask the ruling Socialist party to form a new government later in the day as expected, because of the protests.
He was to meet his advisory National Security Council on Saturday morning to discuss his next move.

Anger at the country's severe economic crisis on Friday spilled over into the worst political violence since the overthrow of one-party rule in 1989. It came after the Socialists decided to form a new government, ignoring opposition calls for a general election.
